main_body: A flat strip of sand ground with sparse darker and lighter speckles, a small grey stone and a pink flower. It is a terrain patch, not a standing object.
top_band: none. The column scan shows only sand speckle (L 169, 198, 220) with no top band and no front face.
evidence: This is a ground tile drawn as a flat surface seen from above, which is correct for terrain. The 3/4 top-and-front contract for standing objects does not apply. No receding side faces and no elevation-style faces are drawn, so nothing violates the view.

style.evidence: The sand uses only three tones (#c9a666, #e2c584, #f1dca2) plus a few accent pixels, 11 colours in total. The median is 3 colours per tile, against 26 for the reference grass and 7 for the reference paving. The speckle is sparse and mostly single pixels on one base tone, so the patch reads as a near-flat wash next to the grass reference, which has layered clumps and tufts. There is no flat-fill block by the 5x5 measure, and it has no outline, which is fine for ground. Even so, the shading depth and tile information density are well below the Beodeul bar.
